newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks pull higher after drop in NAPM index.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks pull higher after drop in NAPM index.

text.p: Wall Street stocks adopted a firmer tone as the bond market strengthened following the release of data which showed a decline in the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) report for June.
The NAPM index showed a reading of 55.7 in June compared with a forecast reading of 56.4 and a reading of 57.1 in May.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up around 20 points to 7692, after shifting between minute gains and losses earlier. Bonds rose 5/32 to a yield of 6.77 percent.
The decline in the NAPM index assuaged financial markets' fears about excessive growth in the manufacturing sector, which might fuel inflation, analysts said.
Both markets were susceptible to inflation and interest rate jitters as the Federal Reserve's rate-setting group of policy makers began a two-day meeting today, they said.

"Two NAPM components -- the prices index and the supplier deliveries index -- considered to be leading indicators of inflation and are closely watched by the Fed...declined," Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany said. "This is very encouraging for bonds and the Fed," he said.
The U.S. Commerce Department reported construction spending fell 1.8 percent in May, versus a forecast rise of 0.5 percent and a decline of one percent the previous month.
The Conference Board index of leading indicators rose 0.3 percent in May versus a decline of 0.1 percent in April.
